{{short description|Scottish statistician (1881–1969)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''David Heron''' (28 April 1881 - 4 November 1969) was a [[Scottish people|Scottish]] [[statistician]]<ref name="Obituary">{{Cite journal|jstor = 2343714|title = David Heron, 1881-1969|journal = Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series A (General)|volume = 133|issue = 2|pages = 287–291|last1 = Pearson|first1 = E. S|year = 1970}}</ref> who was president of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] from 1947 to 1949.

He was born in Perth and studied Mathematics and Natural Philosophy at the University of St Andrews.<ref name="Obituary"/>

He was [[Karl Pearson]]'s research assistant.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Wooldridge |first1=Adrian |title=Measuring the Mind: Education and Psychology in England C.1860-c.1990 |date=2006 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9780521026185 |page=78 |edition=2}}</ref> Later he became a fellow at the Eugenics Laboratory of University College London.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Soloway |first1=Richard A. |title=Demography and Degeneration: Eugenics and the Declining Birthrate in Twentieth-Century Britain |date=2014 |publisher=UNC Press Books |isbn=9781469611198 |page=14}}</ref>

In 1906 he published "On the relation of fertility in man to social status".

In 1915 he became chief statistician for the London Guarantee & Accident Company, an insurance company. During the Second World War, he was Director of Statistics for the Ministry of Food.<ref name="Obituary"/>

He was married to Ethel Medwin from 1916 until her death in 1959.<ref name="Obituary"/>
